conflict_topics: Strong-smelling cooking odor affecting bedrooms, laundry, and work calls
When (which days/times) Agent D may cook strong-smelling food
Whether prior notice or schedule adjustments adequately mitigate the smell
dialogue_quality_notes: Participants provide concrete reasons (work calls, laundry schedule) and propose practical solutions (weekend-only cooking, prior notice, avoiding specific laundry days).
Agent D shifts from defensive to negotiative: initially "it's my food" then later makes scheduling concessions.
There is some repetition: Agent A's final concern is restated almost verbatim (Turn 29 and Turn 32).
Conversation stays on-topic and consistent with the setting (no role confusion).
evaluation.final_reason: Partial accommodations were offered and accepted in the middle of the run (Agent D agreed to notify Agent B and to avoid cooking on Agent C's laundry days — "Okay. I can do that."), but Agent A's main concern (weekday evening video calls until about 7 p.m. and lingering odor) remained unaddressed and was restated in Rounds 11–12 ("if you cook on Tuesdays and Thursdays, the smell is still going to be a problem for my work calls"; "My calls are often until 7 p.m. And the smell stays in the air for hours"). No agreement resolving A's incompatibility with D's cooking times was reached.
position_change_notes: Agent D: moved from defensive ('that's my food. It's what I eat.') to making concrete concessions (agreed to cook on other days and to give B prior notice) — evidence: R2, R5, R8, R10.

Agent A: initially accepted a weekends-only proposal ('That works for me. Thanks, Agent D.' in R6) but later reasserted that weekends or given alternate days still conflict with work hours (R11–R12), showing a position reassessment.
Agent C: consistently concerned about laundry; obtained an explicit concession from D to avoid Mondays/Wednesdays/Fridays (R9–R10).
Agent B: moved from complaint to a minimal accommodation preference (advance notice) which D accepted (R8).

round_scores.evidence: Agent B: "Yeah, my room still smells of it." Agent A: "I have my work calls here in the living room. It's not great when the whole place smells." — initial complaint about cooking smell, no explicit opposition yet.
Agent C: "My laundry smells of it too." vs Agent D: "I hear you, but that's my food. It's what I eat." — explicit incompatible claims (duty to cook preferred food vs request to stop strong smells).
Agent A explains work impact: "I'm on video calls..." Agent D asks a clarifying question: "Okay. When are your calls?" — conflict remains but D engages and seeks information.

Agent A: "They're on weekdays, usually until about 7 p.m." Agent B: "But if she cooks at night, the smell is still there in the morning." — constraints and persistence of odor reiterated; no settlement.
Agent D offers a compromise: "What if I only cook this kind of food on the weekends?" — an attempt to reduce conflict, but no agreement yet from all.
Agent A: "That works for me." then Agent B objects: "But the smell is still there on the weekend." — D's proposed compromise is challenged, raising the level of disagreement again.

Agent C: weekend laundry is affected; Agent D: "Okay, so weekends don't work for you. What's the solution then? Because I can't just not cook my food here." — D asserts inability to stop cooking, showing stronger opposition and entrenchment.
Agent B proposes notice: "Just tell me before you start. If I know, I can close my door." Agent D: "Okay, I can do that, Agent B." — partial accommodation for B but not yet resolving other concerns.

Agent C: "Telling me beforehand doesn't really help... I do my laundry on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays. Could you cook it on the other days?" — a scheduling request that still conflicts with D's practice until D responds.

Agent D agrees to C's request: "Okay. I can do that." Agent C: "Okay, thanks." (At this point there is an explicit accommodation: D accepts to avoid cooking on C's laundry days; B also was offered prior notice.)

Agent A objects again: "Sorry, but if you cook on Tuesdays and Thursdays, the smell is still going to be a problem for my work calls." vs Agent D: "I thought your calls were during the day?" — A's work-schedule concern reintroduces unresolved incompatibility.
Agent A reiterates: "My calls are often until 7 p.m. And the smell stays in the air for hours." — restatement of the unresolved issue; no counterproposal or acceptance recorded.

substantive_insights: The odor lingers for hours, so solutions based solely on day-switching (weekends vs weekdays) may not protect those with evening constraints (A's calls until 7 p.m.).
Advance notice helps some residents (B can close a door) but does not help others (C cannot move hanging laundry).
Agent D is willing to adjust schedule for some housemates (agreed to avoid C's laundry days and to notify B), indicating scope for partial accommodations but not full elimination of conflict.
The core tension is between a resident's cultural/food practices and others' work/laundry needs in a shared, unmodifiable space.
